headline: CHINA 🇨🇳 CENSORS 🛑 Tibet 🌄 Floods 💦 Footage 📹
text:
DRAMATIC 💧 footage 📽️ of a TORRENT 🌊 tearing 🪓 through Gyirong 🏔️ Port 🚪 one of the main border 🚧 crossings between Nepal 🇳🇵 and Tibet 🏔️ sweeping 🧹 away everything in its path 🛤️ as hundreds of people 👥 fled 🏃‍♂️ for their lives 🧬 is almost IMPOSSIBLE 🚫 to miss on social media 📱 around the WORLD 🌍 yet inside China 🇨🇳 you barely see ANYTHING 🕳️!! Only a SINGLE ☝️ still-frame shot 📸 has been broadcast 📺 by the state-run flagship news bulletin 📰 so far and the full video 🎞️ is near IMPOSSIBLE 🚫 to find on the heavily censored internet 🕸️ although various aspects of the disaster 🌋 have been discussed online 💬!! Beijing 🏛️ has launched a massive rescue operation 🛟 involving hundreds of emergency workers 👷‍♂️ which is still continuing 🔄 and President Xi Jinping 👔 chaired an emergency meeting 🪑 to coordinate efforts 🤝 but when you compare the country's internet content 📲 to what the rest of the world 🌍 has been seeing these past few days the firewall 🧱 becomes more visible than EVER 🌟!! Tibet 🏔️ which Beijing annexed in the 1950s has long resisted rule by the Chinese Communist Party 🏛️ and that history means the very name Tibet 🏔️ draws China's censors 🛑 especially at times like this when a barrier lake 🌊 risks overflowing and daily updates on the missing and the dead ⚰️ keep coming but without survivor accounts 🗣️ or user-generated clips 🎥 from inside the region!!

NEW footage 📹 from Chinese state media showed rescue teams 👷‍♂️ wandering in a wasteland of mud 🏜️ and rock 🪨 while calling out 📢 to anyone trapped 🆘 yet there is little detail beyond that no accounts from survivors 🧍‍♂️ in Tibet 🏔️ and almost no user-generated footage 📽️ showing the deadly moments 💥 or their aftermath 🌧️!! We are yet to hear from anxious families 👨‍👩‍👧 of those missing and trying to contact people there is near-impossible during regular times ⏰ as a journalist who has covered North Korea 🇰🇵 it has often been easier to reach interviewees in Pyongyang than in the Tibetan capital Lhasa 🏯!! On Thursday night as global headlines led on the devastation in a Himalayan valley 🏔️ China's state broadcaster opened its main bulletin with the launch of Xi's new book 📖 a selection of his most important and fundamental works instead of focusing on the floods 🌊!! Foreign journalists cannot travel to Tibet 🏔️ without government permission so we have just a few hours to gather information before videos are scrubbed 🧼 and voices stifled 🗣️🔇 forcing us to rely on state media which has focused on incredibly dramatic rescue efforts 🦸‍♂️ scaling mountains 🏔️ and crossing raging rivers 🌊 but we don't know what happened afterwards or who they saved 🙌!!

THIS is not to say that Beijing 🏛️ is unconcerned they are VERY concerned and China's Premier Li Qiang 👔 was quickly despatched to the region where he was seen inspecting debris removal 🧹 a rare visit by the country's second-most important leader so soon after a major disaster 🌪️!! The reason for what the world might see as a muted response is to preserve the one thing Xi covets for his country stability 🧘‍♂️ because the Communist Party 🏛️ will fear that such a disaster could fuel discontent either with the response or the lack of foresight to prevent it and it may also fear the impact of a tragedy like this becoming a rallying factor especially in a community where faith 🙏 has long played a central role!! Although the region has not seen protests in a long time Tibetan groups abroad have expressed concern over increasing Chinese control such as new education laws 📜 that they say aim to weaken the role of monasteries and the Buddhist faith 🛕 and just hours after the disaster struck the Communist Party machine tried to rally its grassroots to stem any signs of discontent of its handling of the landslide 🪨!! A notice came from the local party office urging members to step up and help in disaster relief efforts 🆘 in their area and provide emotional guidance or psychological support to affected residents with the key line instructing them to make every effort to maintain social order and ensure stability and public confidence in the disaster areas 🌍 those who perform well would be rewarded 🏆 and those who do badly would be held accountable ⚖️!!

IT is a warning that will not be taken lightly and Tibetans in the region can be detained or arrested for speaking to journalists 🗣️ or posting anything online that is seen as contrary to the government narrative according to rights activists and that is making it difficult for Tibetans outside the region to find out what has happened to their relatives 👪!! The International Campaign for Tibet while praising the work of first responders 🦸‍♂️ in the area said Beijing had been removing videos 📹 and other first-hand information from social media 📱 and it called on Chinese authorities to disclose complete and verifiable information about the damage and casualties 📊!! To try to understand what life is like for Tibetans the BBC travelled to a town that sits on the edge of the Himalayan plateau last year just outside what China calls the Tibetan Autonomous region where we spoke to monks at the Kirti monastery 🛕 in Aba or Ngaba in Tibetan which was once at the heart of its resistance to Beijing and one monk told us we Tibetans are denied basic human rights 🛑 while they said they lived under constant surveillance 📹 and claimed the Chinese government oppressed and persecuted Tibetans though the conversations were brief because we could not be seen speaking to anyone for long!! Beijing denies it is violating Tibetans rights and points to the heavy investments it has made in the region to boost tourism 🏞️ and integrate it with the rest of the country nevertheless people in China will not know very much about what is happening in Tibet right now 🏔️!!
